report.tagline: A screenless fitness and health band sold only as a membership, which tracks sleep, strain and recovery and tells you how ready your body is each day.
report.simpleSummary: WHOOP is a small band you wear on your wrist all the time. It has no screen, so you check everything in the phone app. Each morning it gives you a Recovery score that says how ready your body is, based on your sleep and heart data, and it tracks how hard you push yourself during the day. You do not buy the band; you pay a yearly membership, from about $199, and the hardware comes with it. It grew fast in 2025 and was valued at $10.1 billion in March 2026.

overview.whatItDoes: WHOOP sells a membership that includes a wearable band and an app. The band measures heart rate, heart rate variability, skin temperature, blood oxygen and movement around the clock. The app turns this into three daily scores: Sleep, Strain and Recovery, plus coaching from an AI assistant. Higher tiers add medical-style features like ECG, Blood Pressure Insights and Healthspan, which estimates your body's pace of ageing. Advanced Labs lets members get blood tests analysed in the app.
howItWorks: A customer picks a membership tier (One, Peak or Life) and gets the band free with the plan.
The band is worn 24/7, with about 14 days of battery and a slide-on charger so it never comes off.
Data syncs to the app, which shows Recovery each morning, Strain during the day and Sleep at night.
WHOOP Coach, an AI assistant, answers questions and gives advice based on the member's data.
Members join teams and challenges, and see how habits like alcohol affect recovery in the Journal.
Members renew yearly; upgrades to new hardware come with the membership.
overview.valueProposition: Know what your body needs today: whether to push hard or rest, and how sleep and habits change your health, without a screen distracting you.

businessModel.summary: WHOOP sells memberships, not devices. Members pay yearly, the band is included, and WHOOP earns more from higher tiers and add-ons like blood tests.

revenueStreams.detail: WHOOP One, Peak and Life, from about $199 to $359 a year in the US.
Bands, clothing with sensor pockets and chargers.
Plans for sports teams, military and companies.

businessModel.pricing: US memberships: WHOOP One about $199 a year, Peak about $239 a year and Life about $359 a year (prices at 2025 launch; check site). One-month free trial.
costDrivers: Regulatory and clinical validation for medical features
businessModel.unitEconomics: A Peak member pays about $239 a year. The band might cost around $40 to $60 to make and ship, though it is replaced only every few years. Cloud and support add a few dollars a month. So WHOOP may keep well over half of that $239 before marketing. Because members open the app eight times a day, many renew, and every renewal year without a new band is very profitable. The risk is people who cancel after the first year before CAC is paid back.

howTheyGetUsers: Athlete ambassadors and investors like Cristiano Ronaldo and LeBron James
growth.moat: WHOOP has 24 billion hours of body data and a brand trusted by athletes, which makes its scores and AI coaching better over time. Members who have years of history and a daily habit are unlikely to switch. Big tech watches and rings offer similar data, so the moat is the habit and the brand, not the sensor.

northStar.metric: Members who wear the band at least 6 nights a week and check Recovery

strengths: Very high engagement, 8+ app opens a day
Recurring membership revenue and cash flow positive

No screen for live workout data
Communication missteps, like the 2025 upgrade fee backlash

Apple, Samsung and Garmin adding similar recovery scores free

improvementIdeas.idea: Publish a clear hardware upgrade promise tied to membership length
Monthly pay option for WHOOP One to lower the barrier
Weekly AI Coach plan that suggests one habit to change with a predicted Recovery impact
improvementIdeas.problem: Members see data but do not know what to do.

improvementIdeas.idea: Accuracy reports comparing WHOOP to clinical measures, shown in the app

pmLessons: Selling the outcome (daily guidance) instead of the device makes a subscription feel worth it.
A single daily score can create a habit. Recovery is why people open WHOOP eight times a day.
Changing promises to paying members, like upgrade terms, can quickly break trust.
Moving from fitness to health raises prices but also brings regulators.

interviewQuestions.question: Why would someone pay $239 a year for WHOOP when a Garmin has no subscription?
interviewQuestions.hint: Focus on value: coaching, upgrades, habit; segment who it is for; discuss pricing psychology.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you increase renewal after year one?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find churn drivers, link to engagement, design interventions like yearly recap and new features, measure renewal.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a WHOOP feature for women's health.
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick a need (cycle, pregnancy, menopause), use existing sensors, define the metric and guardrails.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you handle the WHOOP 5.0 upgrade backlash as PM?
interviewQuestions.hint: Acknowledge, segment affected members, offer clear options, measure sentiment and renewals.

interviewQuestions.question: What should WHOOP's north star metric be?
interviewQuestions.hint: Consistent wear plus daily Recovery check, explain why it beats revenue or downloads.
